summary: The note argues that tech mentorship programs are vital for at-risk youth, but that they suffer from a shortage of female mentors. It describes how female mentors provide role models for girls and boys, challenge stereotypes, and help shift tech culture. It cites new initiatives like TechGals, a December 2023 report, and quotes from mentors, and calls on programs to recruit and support more women.
one_line: Tech mentorship programs for at-risk youth need more female mentors, who widen participation, challenge stereotypes and help make tech more inclusive.
key_facts: Since September 2023 there has been a surge in mentorship efforts for at-risk youth in tech, but female mentors remain underrepresented.
Sarah Johnson, a software engineer at a top tech firm and mentor in a local tech education program, spoke on October 15, 2023 about girls believing certain aspects of tech are 'not for girls'.
TechGals is an organization established in November 2023 that focuses solely on connecting female tech professionals with local community tech programs for at-risk youth.
TechGals founder Emily Rodriguez said that when young people see a woman excelling in a tech career, 'it shifts their understanding of who belongs in tech.'
The National Alliance for Youth Tech Education released a report on December 1, 2023 showing a positive correlation between diverse mentorship and student outcomes.
The report found programs with more female mentors saw increased girls' participation and interest in advanced subjects such as AI development and cybersecurity.
A group mentored by engineer Sophia Martinez developed a community app providing resources for families in need.
Sophia Martinez said on January 20, 2024 that homogeneous groups working on tech solutions miss out on the creative solutions diversity brings.
Women in tech named as exemplars include Sheryl Sandberg, Ginni Rometty, and Reshma Saujani.
Initiatives promoting female mentorship in tech programs were launched in urban and rural communities throughout the last quarter of 2023.
Beyond coding, the programs foster critical thinking, problem-solving, and project management skills.
The note urges existing tech programs to proactively recruit and support more female mentors and to encourage women in tech to take on these roles.
